purpose: Catalog everything Phase 3F.1.5.1 did NOT close, so its ENVIRONMENT_BLOCKED verdict is not mistaken for progress toward a pass on the underlying gate.

primaryUnresolvedItem.criterion: Independent second-pass adjudication agreement (Phase 3F.1.5's criterion H)
primaryUnresolvedItem.status: STILL MISSED, and NOT re-tested in this phase
primaryUnresolvedItem.detail: The original 78.4%/84.3% binary and 37.3% detailed agreement numbers stand completely unchanged. This phase produced a rigorous forensic explanation for WHY they came in low (01-original-disagreement-forensics.json) and a designed-but-unexecuted fix (02-state-taxonomy.json, 05-second-pass-protocol.json, 06-frozen-sample.json, 07-preregistered-agreement-computation.json), but explicitly did not - and, per the phase's own charter, could not responsibly - execute a rerun to test whether that fix actually works, because the mandated rerun order requires live semantic judgment first and no authorized model credential exists in this environment (04-live-semantic-judge-run.json).

newFindingsFromThisPhase.finding: 65.6% of the original 32 detailed disagreements (21 of 32) are pure state-taxonomy vocabulary mismatches with zero credit-direction disagreement, not genuine evaluator/reviewer disagreement.
newFindingsFromThisPhase.confidence: HIGH - directly computed from frozen data, not inferred.
newFindingsFromThisPhase.implication: The true severity of Phase 3F.1.5's methodology gap is smaller than the raw 37.3% detailed-agreement number suggested, but this does not change the gate outcome: the pre-registered thresholds were defined against the ORIGINAL vocabulary, and this phase does not retroactively reinterpret that result as a pass.

newFindingsFromThisPhase.finding: doc-a::VI::6.10-chapeau, one of the 14 confirmed Phase 3F.1.1 false credits, was independently re-credited by the blinded Phase 3F.1.5 second-pass reviewer, who was not told about its false-credit history.
newFindingsFromThisPhase.implication: This is concrete evidence that V2's stricter discovery-vs-compiled-representation design choice is protecting against a real, previously-demonstrated failure mode, and that a future, more lenient second-pass protocol (or a future live semantic judge) risks reproducing this specific defect if not carefully instructed. Any future protocol revision must be validated against this specific case before being trusted.

newFindingsFromThisPhase.finding: A previously-undetected, repeatable V2_LOGIC_DEFECT: the compiled 'Acquisition' IR-definition candidate (ir-definition:007a5206...) was granted PARTIAL credit against three unrelated Section-1.01 definitional GT claims (facility sizes, net income, supply-chain financing) with near-identical boilerplate reasoning.
newFindingsFromThisPhase.confidence: HIGH - three independent instances of the identical pattern in the same frozen sample.
newFindingsFromThisPhase.implication: This is a genuine residual defect in V2's own correspondence layer for definitional/economic-metric claims - the second-pass gate did exactly what it was designed to do by catching it. NOT fixed in this phase, per the explicit no-rewrite-after-seeing-results rule. Should be the first item addressed in a future V2 code iteration, tracked as an open defect.

newFindingsFromThisPhase.finding: Two cases (doc-a::X::10.01a-us-guaranty, doc-a::X::10.06-reinstatement) show internally inconsistent characterization of the SAME candidate ID (ir-rule:8543f9e7... and ir-rule:fb5206d4...) across different second-pass case narratives - described as 'Section 1.07 subordination' in two cases and as 'election of remedies / no prior action' in a third.
newFindingsFromThisPhase.confidence: MEDIUM - the inconsistency is directly observed, but its root cause (a V2 correspondence-layer defect, a second-pass reading error, or genuinely multi-topic candidate content) is not determined.
newFindingsFromThisPhase.implication: Carried forward, unresolved, exactly as flagged in Phase 3F.1.5's own remaining-risks artifact. This is the single most concrete lead for a future direct excerpt-level investigation - it should not wait for a full rerun; a targeted read of these two candidate IDs' actual excerpt content could resolve it cheaply, at zero model cost, in a future session with tool access to re-examine (not alter) the frozen fixture data.

stillOpenFromPhase3F15: No live semantic AI judge has EVER been executed in this codebase's history, across two consecutive phases now (3F.1.5 and 3F.1.5.1). Both independently confirmed no authorized model credential is available in their respective execution environments. This is now a two-phase-confirmed blocker, not a one-off environment fluke - a future iteration should not assume the environment will differ without a fresh, direct check exactly like the one performed here.

newGapIntroducedByThisPhase: A precise discoveryRecall and safeSurfacingRate metric (distinct from the conflated honestUnresolvedOrUnsupportedRate) was designed in the state taxonomy but not computed, since computing it would require re-deriving from frozen evidence under a metric definition invented after the original numbers were already seen - itself a form of post-hoc metric engineering this phase's charter prohibits. This is deliberately left as a designed-but-uncalculated gap for the SAME future iteration that executes the live-judge rerun, not calculated retroactively here.
